derived_claims: It tracks the long-term trajectory of a major industrial air pollutant across nearly three centuries, mapping the shifting geographic centers of industrial activity.
global emissions remained extremely low until the mid-19th century, after which they rose exponentially, peaking around 1980 at approximately 140 million tonnes.

post-1980, emissions from these regions declined sharply, while emissions from Asia grew rapidly, reflecting a shift in heavy industrial manufacturing and coal consumption.
By 2022, global emissions had fallen to roughly half of their peak levels, driven largely by the clean-up of Western energy sectors and, more recently, Chinese mitigation efforts.
speculative_claims: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) is primarily released through the combustion of sulfur-containing fossil fuels (like coal and oil) and industrial processes like metal smelting.

The dramatic decline in North American and European SO₂ emissions since the 1970s and 1980s is widely attributed to the implementation of strict environmental regulations, such as the Clean Air Act, and the adoption of flue-gas desulfurization technologies (scrubbers) in power plants.
Reducing SO₂ is critical because it is a primary precursor to acid rain, which deforests ecosystems and acidifies waterways, and it poses severe risks to human respiratory health.
The ongoing emissions in regions like Asia and Africa highlight the modern challenge of balancing rapid economic development and energy access with environmental and public health protections.
